title: Outlook: declarative agents in Copilot Chat in classic Outlook for Windows
notes: claim 52: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
claim 53: severity major on a rationale: impact rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Held because the Teams availability path omits its app-centric-management prerequisite: tenants still using permission policies cannot follow that route as written. Three descriptive claims also go beyond the documentation, while the roadmap facts, licensing rules and API calls are supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go agents are off by default for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users.
claims.quote: Pay-as-you-go agents are turned off by default for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) users

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Agents grounded in instructions and public websites are included with Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and (Premium).
claims.quote: Declarative agents that are grounded in instructions and public websites are included with Copilot Chat (Basic), and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) and (Premium).

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed, combining included agents and metered shared-tenant-data agents for Basic licences.
claims.quote: Agents that use public data are available for Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) licenses. Access to agents that use shared tenant data are pay-as-you-go only.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: cost
claims.claim: For Basic licences, agents accessing shared tenant data such as SharePoint or Graph Connector content are billed by metered consumption.
claims.quote: For Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 (Basic) licenses, agents that access shared tenant data, such as SharePoint or Graph Connector content, are billed based on metered consumption.

claims.claim: Metered agents require setting up or using an existing Copilot Studio subscription.
claims.quote: You must set up or use an existing Copilot Studio subscription.

claims.claim: Agent use comes with the Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) licence.
claims.quote: The use of agents comes with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license.

claims.claim: No enabling action is needed for Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) agents.
claims.quote: No action is needed to enable agents for Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium).

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go setup in the Microsoft 365 admin center requires an Azure subscription in the Microsoft 365 tenant.
claims.quote: You must have an Azure subscription in the same tenant as Microsoft 365. If you don't have an Azure subscription, you can create one during the billing policy setup process.

claims.claim: A budget on a pay-as-you-go billing policy triggers email notifications.
claims.quote: When you set a budget amount, it triggers email notifications based on your organization's spending relative to that limit.

claims.claim: The budget is not enforced and does not prevent spending above it.
claims.quote: However, the system doesn't enforce the budget or prevent your organization from exceeding it. Usage can continue uninterrupted even after the budget is surpassed, ensuring no disruption to the service.

claims.claim: Turning pay-as-you-go off can take up to two hours to stop users using agents.
claims.quote: When you turn off pay-as-you-go, it can take up to two hours for users to stop being able to use the agents. If the agent is unused, it stops being available when pay-as-you-go is turned off.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The tenant-wide block control is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > All agents > agent > Block.
claims.quote: Select Agents > All agents. In the All agents page, select an agent from the list of agents. In the agent details pane that opens, immediately under the agent's name, select Block or Unblock.

claims.claim: POST /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block blocks a Copilot package to prevent its use.
claims.quote:
Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects their availability and functionality in Outlook and other host products.
claims.quote: Blocking or unblocking an agent that you created by using Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and Microsoft Copilot Studio affects its availability and functionality in Microsoft Copilot. It also affects availability and functionality in other host products, such as Microsoft Outlook

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry agents only impacts availability in Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The printed Teams admin center availability path is presented without requiring migration to app-centric management.
claims.quote: All organizations don't have the app centric management feature available. If you see policies on the permission policies page, continue to use app permission policies or migrate to this feature on your own.
claims.fix: Keep the path, but prepend this sentence to controls[1].note and add it before the Teams path guidance: 'The Teams admin center path requires app-centric management; tenants still using app permission policies must continue using those policies or migrate to app-centric management.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management. This prerequisite is distinct from unified app management.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id} updates which users or groups can access the package.
The update request body uses availableTo and allowedUsersAndGroups to set availability.
claims.quote:
allowedUsersAndGroups: Users/groups for whom the package is available.
availableTo: Enum value specifying which users or groups within the tenant can access this package.

claims.claim: availableTo is required when updating allowedUsersAndGroups.
claims.quote: availableTo: Enum value specifying which users or groups within the tenant can access this package. Required if updating allowedUsersAndGroups.

claims.claim: Every agent the catalogue offers to Copilot Chat users is now one click from their mail and calendar in classic Outlook.
claims.quote: Searched: 'classic Outlook Copilot Chat agents all agents'. Opened release-notes and agents-overview. The release note documents declarative agents and interaction with available agents, not every catalogue agent or a universal one-click experience.
claims.fix: Replace 'so every agent your catalogue offers to Copilot Chat users is now one click from their mail and calendar' with 'so the declarative agent experience is now available within their mailbox client'.

claims.claim: Agents with the documented Outlook integrations provide actions and assistance from within the mailbox client.
claims.quote: Extending agent integrated extensibility experience support to classic Outlook for Windows allows more users to benefit from automated assistance and task management within their familiar email environment leveraging extensibility provider agent actions and orchestration logic.

claims.claim: The classic Outlook release note does not describe whether agent actions require user confirmation.
claims.quote: Searched: 'classic Outlook agents confirm 481559'. Read the complete 481559 entry in release-notes, including What changed, Why and Try this. It lists actions but does not state whether confirmation is required.

claims.claim: The cited feature release note does not identify the first classic Outlook build carrying this experience.
claims.quote: Searched: 'classic Outlook declarative agents build mail flow' and '481559 build'. Read the 481559 release-notes entry and roadmap record. Neither gives a build number; the targeted searches returned no feature-specific build requirement.

claims.claim: Copilot Chat users in classic Outlook encounter the agent experience in chat.
claims.quote: Access Copilot Chat from the ribbon or sidebar. Interact with available Copilot agents to automate tasks or get assistance.

claims.claim: Mail flow is not changed by this item.

claims.claim: The rest of Outlook is not changed by this item.

claims.fix: Remove 'mail flow and the rest of Outlook are not changed by this item' from the impact rationale.
